summary: Tested encrypted backups (.vbk) with a required Backup Password, on both backend and frontend. Backend: 11 pytest cases in a new suite, 10 pass. Covered: the must_set_backup_password flags on login and /auth/me; /backup/security; /backup/auto (file starts with 9XVBK and has no readable JSON); GET /backup (octet-stream, *_download.vbk); restore-file errors (wrong password, missing password, path traversal and bad names give 404) and success with data unchanged; multipart restore (wrong, missing and correct password, plain text file, {foo:1} JSON); /backup/password checks (422, missing, wrong current, wrong login); change to a temporary password, then revert through the forgot flow (an old .vbk still opens with the old password, a new one needs the new password); file list sorting and flags; 401 without auth. The unit tests (test_backup_crypto + test_security) pass 14/14. One bug: a truncated .vbk upload causes a 500 error. Frontend: every requested flow passes. Covered: login goes to the dashboard with no gate; the Backup page header and BackupPasswordCard status; form fields, the forgot toggle and both validation toasts; Backup Now toast and the 'Encrypted · test hint' lock column; the restore dialog (button disabled until a password is typed, wrong-password toast keeps the dialog open, cancel, correct password restores and reloads with counts unchanged); download event with the right filename and 9XVBK file start; upload restore with the downloaded file (wrong, then correct password); Settings shows the card under ChangePasswordCard; Year-end page loads; sidebar logout makes the 'Auto backup ban gaya: ...logout.vbk' backup and goes to /login. Gate test: I deleted db.backup_key. After that the API returns 409 for backup/auto and GET /backup, /auth/me returns must_set_backup_password=true, and setting 'admin123' is rejected. In the UI the gate page appears after login, has no current-password field, and also blocks going straight to /backup. Logout from the gate works. Setting Backup@2026 / 'test hint' lands on the dashboard and survives a reload. FINAL STATE: the backup key exists with password Backup@2026 and hint 'test hint' (checked by the pytest revert step and in Mongo). Login password is unchanged.

minor.issue: A file that starts with the 5-byte magic '9XVBK' but is shorter than the 36-byte header (truncated or corrupt .vbk) returns 500 Internal Server Error. Cause: bkc.unpack -> parse_header raises bkc.NotVbk, and _decode_backup only catches bkc.WrongPassword. Fix: in _decode_backup catch bkc.NotVbk (and zlib.error / ValueError) and raise HTTPException(400, '<name> 9x Vyapari backup nahi hai / file kharab hai').

issues: BackupPasswordCard is full width while the Settings and ChangePasswordCard cards above it are narrower, so the column looks uneven
Settings and Year-end still use the browser's native date inputs (existing issue)
The 'Restored: ...' toast lists all 18 collections, including archive_*:0, which is long and noisy. Consider showing only non-zero counts or a short summary.

action_items: Catch bkc.NotVbk (and zlib/json decode errors) in _decode_backup so a truncated or corrupt .vbk returns 400 instead of 500.

Run the scrypt calls (derive_key, key_matches, unpack, pack) in a threadpool (fastapi.concurrency.run_in_threadpool). They use about 32MB and 100ms of CPU each and currently block the async event loop.
critical_code_review_comments: Security design: db.backup_key stores the actual derived AES key (hex), and every .vbk uses that same salt (the docstring says 'per-file salt', but pack() always gets k['salt']). Anyone who can read the local MongoDB, which has no auth, can decrypt every backup without the password. Only a stolen backup file on its own is protected. Options: store only a verifier and wrap a random data key, or use a public-key scheme so auto-backups can be encrypted without the password while decrypting still needs it.

APP_SECRET is built from plain strings in the source (backup_crypto._PARTS), so it is obfuscation, not a real secret. Anyone who has the code or reverse-engineers the Electron build gets it. The real protection is the user's password plus scrypt, which is fine, but avoid overstating the 'only this software' claim.

Old plain JSON files are still accepted by /api/restore and /api/backup/restore-file. A hand-made JSON with a 'data' key can overwrite the whole DB with no schema check. Consider rejecting JSON once a backup password is set, or at least checking the expected keys.
_restore_all is not transactional (delete_many then insert_many for each collection). If an insert fails partway, data is lost. Make an automatic safety backup ('pre-restore') before any restore.
Test and manual backups count toward BACKUP_KEEP=30, so repeated test runs push out real logout and year-end backups. The folder is at 30 files now.
The backup-password gate is frontend-only. All data APIs still work while must_set_backup_password=true; only backup creation returns 409. Acceptable, but note it.
server.py is 2720 lines. The backup and year-end sections could move to their own modules.

rca of the issue: Truncated .vbk gives 500. Repro: curl -F file=@<(printf 9XVBK);filename=t.vbk -F password=Backup@2026 /api/restore -> 500. is_vbk() passes on the magic bytes, then parse_header raises NotVbk because len < _FIXED_LEN, and _decode_backup only catches WrongPassword. Fix: add 'except bkc.NotVbk as e: raise HTTPException(400, str(e))'.
